sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh) 末昂语 and (en) Maang language, raw wikitext, accessed 2026-09-17
sources.note: Secondary; phonology paragraph (from Zhou 2014) lists initials/finals/tones only; no stress. Reference lists used to identify Wu 1993, Zhou 2014, Wang 2018, Lama 2012, Hsiu 2014/2017.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14). Taipei: Academia Sinica. 20 pp.
sources.note: Comparative subgrouping paper; Maang data taken from Lama (2012), Longyang village; forms carry tone numbers; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing). Notes that Wu Zili (1993) was the first documentation of Mo'ang.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14)

sources.note: 175 wav files + wordlist from Dala village, Napo County (Meang variety); no stress information.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages: A Study from the Perspectives of Shared Innovation and Phylogenetic Estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: pp. 84-85 (pdf 103-104): 'Maang has 36 initials, 63 vowels (20 monophthongs, 20 diphthongs, 2 triphthongs, 17 finals with nasal codas, and 4 finals with stop codas), and 5 tones (/55/, /44/, /33/, /35/, and /21/) (LM Self-data 2003).' No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the dissertation (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.access_detail: online with restricted access (login, paywall or limited view)
sources.note: Cross-Ngwi (Loloish) study of the change *high tone > rising tone. Crossref abstract: 'Among the 11 Ngwi language clusters examined, a new rising tone value has unambiguously developed from an historically high tone in nine of them. In several clusters, prevocalic consonants conditioned a tone split, but in other clusters, *high > rising appears after both voiced and voiceless prevocalic consonants.' Maang (maan1239, 'Yunnan Wenshan Funing', source label YYFC1983) is one of 76 doculects in the open CLDF supplement (lexibank/yangyi v1.3); its 229 forms carry five tone values, by syllable count…
